alignments.note: Waw rendered by the connective *Now* under rule 14; the list of connectives is read off the ASV.
Presentative הָיָה with its dummy subject frame under rules 21 and 45; the frame's *that* is not here, since the apodosis opens with its own waw (s014), which carries it. Head on the lexical *came*.
Article to the written *the* (rule 15).
הַיּוֹם is a bare adverbial accusative with no preposition on it, so the supplied *on* belongs to the noun whose case-function licenses it (rule 33). Head on *day* by rule 31.
The ASV recasts this waw's clause as a temporal subordinate clause and writes only *when* for it (rules 14 and 55); no separate *and* is written, so the unit takes just the subordinator.
Finite verb to *came*; its subject is the explicit nominal, so no pronoun joins it (rule 17).
Construct noun takes only its own word; the relation's *of* goes to the rectum by rule 19.
The rectum's own article takes the single written *the*, which English fronts to the phrase's left edge and renders the rectum anarthrously (rule 29).
Nomen rectum with the construct relation's *of*, headed on the noun (rules 19 and 24).
לְ before an infinitive construct with a written *to* (rule 52).
Hithpael infinitive; the reflexive *themselves* renders the verb's own voice and stays in its unit under rule 44. Head on the lexical *present*.
Preposition עַל rendered *before* (rule 11).
Divine name to *Jehovah*.

The apodosis waw carries the presentative frame's *that* under rule 45, which is why s002 keeps only *it came to pass*. The competing reading gives the *that* to הָיָה and marks this waw unrepresented; rule 45's apodosis clause decides it, since the waw is written here.
Finite verb to *came*.
The adverb גַּם takes the written *also*; here a גַּם is present, so rule 51's waw case is not in play.
The ASV writes no *the* for הַשָּׂטָן, rendering it as the name *Satan*, so the article is unrepresented under rule 29. The marginal note *That is, the Adversary* is apparatus, not the aligned text.
Noun rendered as the name *Satan*.

בְּתוֹךְ rendered by the single English word *among*, so the preposition and the construct noun share one unit under rule 30, exactly as לִפְנֵי → *before*; headed on the morpheme carrying the lexeme. The alternative of giving *among* to בְּ alone and marking תָּוֶךְ unrepresented would leave a lexical noun's rendering unaligned against rule 2.
Pronominal suffix as the rectum, rendered by the bare pronoun *them*; the ASV writes no *of* here, so rule 18 governs rather than rule 19's *of them* treatment.

review_notes: The *on* of *on the day* is placed on יוֹם as rule 33's adverbial accusative, since no preposition morpheme stands on הַיּוֹם.
The frame's *that* is given to the apodosis waw s014 under rule 45 rather than to the presentative הָיָה.
בְּתוֹךְ is fused as one unit under rule 30's one-English-word condition.
